title: Classical Mechanics
subject: Mechanics
summary: An intermediate-to-graduate treatment of classical mechanics following Thornton and Marion: Newtonian dynamics with drag and oscillations, calculus of variations and Lagrangian mechanics, central forces, rotating frames, rigid bodies, normal modes, Hamiltonian mechanics and chaos, plus graduate units on Poisson brackets, canonical transformations, Hamilton-Jacobi theory and action-angle variables that lead directly into quantum mechanics and statistical mechanics.

units.title: Newtonian Foundations: Coordinates, Momentum, Angular Momentum, Energy
units.summary: Re-derive the Newtonian toolkit at the level the Lagrangian formalism will build on: vector and polar-coordinate dynamics, momentum and angular-momentum conservation for systems, and work-energy with potential-energy diagrams (the same diagrams a chemist uses for bond potentials).

lessons.title: Newton's laws, inertial frames and momentum conservation
objectives: State Newton's three laws and explain why the first law asserts the existence of inertial frames rather than being a special case of the second.
Show how the third law gives conservation of the total momentum of an isolated pair of particles.

Apply Newton's second law in polar coordinates to solve a bead-on-a-rotating-wire or circular-motion problem.
